useful_delta: Recovered and separated Prometeo's checkpoint/restart semantics into evidence-grounded candidate concepts: RELEASE is a target-confirmed authority checkpoint; WORK_CHECKPOINT is an in-progress continuity snapshot with no promotion semantics; a ZIP is only an emergency restart carrier; working heads remain distinct from target-confirmed heads; rollback preserves newer history while resuming from a confirmed base; forward update reconciles preserved work onto current authority and requires fresh validation before promotion.

RELEASE.definition: A durable checkpoint whose intended target has been positively confirmed and whose authority/provenance is explicit. It is suitable as a canonical restart/rollback anchor for the confirmed scope.
minimum_semantics: Explicit source lineage and authority scope.
A target-confirmed head rather than merely the newest working commit.
Evidence of the relevant confirmation gate, such as served/public target verification, accepted integration target, or another scope-specific target receipt.
No implicit equivalence between being present on main, Human Accepted, Current, Served, or released; each state remains separately evidenced.
non_implications: A newer commit does not automatically supersede a release.
A candidate or integrated artifact is not automatically Human Accepted or Served.
A release for one scope does not confer release authority on unrelated scopes.

WORK_CHECKPOINT.definition: A portable, durable continuity snapshot of work in progress. It exists to resume, transfer, inspect, or recover work without claiming release, acceptance, served state, or canonical authority.
minimum_semantics: Optional rollback base and forward-update candidate references.
Explicit statement that restoration requires revalidation against current authority.
WORK_CHECKPOINT.promotion_rule: A WORK_CHECKPOINT may inform a later RELEASE only after reconciliation and target confirmation. The checkpoint itself never promotes anything.

zip_restart_carrier.role: Emergency/offline restart carrier, not an authority source.
recommended_payload: A manifest identifying the carrier schema/version and creation time.
One WORK_CHECKPOINT for the preserved in-progress frontier.
A reference or copy of the last known RELEASE/rollback base when available.
Survival-set/bootstrap material sufficient to rediscover live authority.
Source/commit identities and checksums for packaged material.
A restore instruction that requires fresh EPOCH/authority/collision validation before writes.
zip_restart_carrier.restore_rule: Unpack as evidence/candidate state. First rediscover stable bootstrap, latest EPOCH, canonical authority and current repository heads; then compare the carrier's release/work heads to live state. Never let ZIP contents overwrite newer authority merely because the carrier is self-contained.
zip_restart_carrier.security_and_freshness_rule: Treat an old or externally moved ZIP as stale/untrusted until checksums, source lineage and authority references are verified. Secrets/private transcript payloads should not be required for the public restart carrier.
zip_restart_carrier.historical_boundary: No tracked PROMETEO.zip artifact or exact current-tree literal was found during this scout. Therefore ZIP is specified here as the recovered emergency-carrier role requested by WI-BIG-11, not asserted as a currently versioned canonical artifact.

head_distinctions.working_head: Newest durable head carrying in-progress work for a run/branch/scope. It may be ahead of canonical or published runtime and can be captured in a WORK_CHECKPOINT, but freshness alone gives it no release authority.
head_distinctions.target_confirmed_head: A head for which the intended target state has positive evidence at the relevant gate. This is the head eligible to anchor a RELEASE or rollback base for that scope.
head_distinctions.published_runtime_head: The source head named by the currently served/materialized runtime/EPOCH. It can lag repository main; publication lag must be diagnosed rather than confused with loss of source work.
head_distinctions.canonical_source_head: Current source authority for the relevant scope after resync. It may differ from both a worker's working head and the served runtime head.
head_distinctions.selection_rule: Never use max(commit time/version number) as an authority rule. Select by scope-specific authority plus confirmation evidence.

rollback.definition: Resume execution or serving from a known target-confirmed release/rollback base without deleting the newer working lineage.
rules: Prefer non-destructive repoint/resume/redeploy semantics over history rewriting.
Record the rollback base and the abandoned/suspended working head separately.
Preserve newer work as a forward-update candidate unless explicitly rejected/superseded by authority.
A capability-proven older donor can be a rollback base for the capability it actually proves; donor status is scoped, not global.

forward_update.definition: Reconcile preserved post-release work onto the latest canonical authority, then validate it again before any release promotion.
rules: Classify differences as already integrated, still useful, conflicting, obsolete, or unsupported.
Rebase/merge/apply only collision-free and still-authorized deltas through the normal owner/steward mechanism.
Run the relevant target confirmation gate on the reconciled head.
Only the newly confirmed head may become the next RELEASE; the pre-confirmation result remains a working/forward-update candidate.

named_concepts_informed.name: release_checkpoint
named_concepts_informed.meaning: Target-confirmed durable authority checkpoint for a defined scope.

named_concepts_informed.name: work_checkpoint
named_concepts_informed.meaning: Portable in-progress continuity snapshot with no acceptance/release implications.

named_concepts_informed.name: restart_carrier
named_concepts_informed.meaning: Portable container such as ZIP that transports checkpoints/survival material but carries no independent authority.

named_concepts_informed.name: target_confirmed_head
named_concepts_informed.meaning: Head with positive target-specific confirmation evidence.

named_concepts_informed.name: working_head
named_concepts_informed.meaning: Newest in-progress head, explicitly non-authoritative until reconciled/confirmed.

named_concepts_informed.name: rollback_base
named_concepts_informed.meaning: Scoped target-confirmed head selected to resume a known-good state.

named_concepts_informed.name: forward_update_candidate
named_concepts_informed.meaning: Preserved newer work awaiting reconciliation against current canonical authority.

named_concepts_informed.name: restore_revalidation
named_concepts_informed.meaning: Mandatory rediscovery of EPOCH, authority, heads and collisions before restored checkpoint material can write or promote.

facts: Historical execution/copy handoff checkpoints already preserve durable continuation state independently from final acceptance/publication.
Historical Study Library markers distinguish source/main state from publication/served state instead of treating them as one boolean release state.
Rehydration material distinguishes candidate, Human Accepted and Served authority and preserves older capability-proven rollback donors without promoting them globally.
The current control-plane architecture treats durable source facts and explicit return/consumption decisions as authority inputs; existence of a RETURN never implies integration or Human Acceptance.

At completion-time pre-write validation, published EPOCH P3-bffc5980ddae named main 298316bd3380 while repository main was 47a38b080012e99c13376d30e5837b08a2d2f033; convergence contained no blocking=true event. This is concrete evidence that published/runtime and working/source heads may legitimately differ.
candidates: Adopt RELEASE and WORK_CHECKPOINT as separate machine-readable checkpoint kinds rather than overloading one checkpoint status.
Represent restart carriers with an explicit authority=false / requires_restore_revalidation=true semantic rather than letting a ZIP masquerade as canonical state.
Persist target_confirmed_head, working_head, rollback_base and forward_update_candidate as distinct references where restart/update flows need them.
Require restore_revalidation before any post-restore material write or release promotion.

evidence.supports: A checkpoint can preserve current execution continuity/frontier without asserting final release or publication.
Copy/handoff checkpointing is used as continuity transport between executions rather than as automatic authority promotion.
Historical release state separates source/main and served/public confirmation.
Release lineage is recorded explicitly rather than inferred from newest version.
Publication confirmation has its own checkpoint/evidence boundary.
Historical publication handling explicitly avoided force semantics, aligning with non-destructive rollback/update.
Restart/rehydration depends on explicit source identities and authority-bearing wake material.
Candidate/Human Accepted/Served distinctions and capability-scoped rollback donor semantics.
There is already a minimal public-safe survival/bootstrap set suitable for inclusion/reference by an emergency restart carrier.
Completion-time runtime revalidation: EPOCH can lag repository main and no blocking collision was present for this scoped return.

unresolved: The exact historical binary/package layout named PROMETEO.zip was not found as a tracked current-tree artifact during this scout. A future implementation pass should recover any off-repo/older carrier manifest if it still exists before standardizing byte-level ZIP layout.

Scope-specific target confirmation gates differ by artifact class; this scout defines the generic distinction but does not collapse Served, Human Accepted, test-passed and other domain confirmations into one universal gate.
suggested_parent_action: Integrate these concepts into the control-plane design as a checkpoint/restart vocabulary layer: RELEASE != WORK_CHECKPOINT; ZIP/restart_carrier has no authority; distinguish target_confirmed_head from working_head; make rollback non-destructive; require restore_revalidation and fresh target confirmation for forward updates. Do not promote any candidate solely from this scout return.
